name: Mizraim
title: Ancestor of the Egyptians
summary: Mizraim was the son of Ham and the grandson of Noah. He is regarded as the ancestor of the Egyptians and several other peoples in North Africa and the eastern Mediterranean region. The Hebrew name "Mitsrajim" is used in the Bible to refer to Egypt.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the genealogy after the Flood
keyEvents.description: Misrajim is mentioned as one of Ham's four sons in the genealogy after Noah in Genesis.

keyEvents.title: The descendants of Misrajim
keyEvents.description: The sons of Misrajim and the nations that descended from him are listed, including the Ludites, Anamites, Lehabites, Naphtuhites, Pathrusites, Casluhites, and Caphtorimtes.

keyEvents.title: Repeated in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: The genealogy from Genesis is repeated in 1 Chronicles, where Misrajim is again mentioned as a son of Ham and the ancestor of several nations.

keyEvents.title: Ham's curse and its context
keyEvents.description: The background for Ham's lineage, including Misrajim, is linked to the event where Noah cursed Canaan after the Flood.

keyEvents.title: The dispersion of the nations
keyEvents.description: Misrajim and his descendants were part of the dispersion of the nations over the earth after the Flood, as described in the table of nations.
